node.label: Tzvetan Todorov
node.date_label: 1982 La Conquête de l’Amérique · 1984 The Conquest of America — Richard Howard’s English translation · 1991 Face à l’extrême
node.description: Tzvetan Todorov connected literary and semiotic inquiry with historical questions about conquest, moral choice and collective memory. La Conquête de l’Amérique uses the encounter between Europeans and Americans to examine relations with others; his short 1984 essay explicitly chooses Mexico as its historical case. Later works address extreme violence and wartime France. In his own essay on memory, commemoration does not automatically prevent renewed violence: narratives of past victimhood can also legitimate aggression. These selected arguments retain their ethical and interpretive character.

proposed_edges.relationship: Uses conquest as a historical case for examining attitudes toward other societies
proposed_edges.evidence_note: The three authored opening paragraphs of “The Morality of Conquest, ” printed 89, explicitly identify the conquest of Mexico and its texts as the case. This limited methodological connection does not assert the unread book’s full thesis or label Todorov a member of a later school.

proposed_edges.relationship: Challenges the assumption that remembering victimhood necessarily prevents violence
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own UNESCO essay distinguishes selective remembrance from ethical use and warns that former victims can become aggressors. This is his bounded intervention on public memory, not a psychological finding or a universal judgment on victims.
